question: Which country gave the world its FIRST vaccine?

post.premise: A country doctor, a milkmaid's hand and an 8-year-old boy
post.bait: France, China or England — which did you pick? 👇
post.sources_line: WHO; Jenner Museum; Riedel 2005 (Proc Bayl Univ Med Cent); Britannica

youtube.title: Where was the first vaccine in history given? A milkmaid's hand started it 💉
youtube.description:
France, China or the third one? In 1796 a country doctor scratched pus from a milkmaid's hand into an 8-year-old's arm, then deliberately exposed the boy to smallpox. Nothing happened — and a disease that killed 3 in 10 of its victims was on its way out.
Guess before the flag lifts, then see the village, the word he coined from Latin, and the day the WHO declared the disease gone.
Which country did you pick?

threads.text: Which country gave the world its first vaccine — France, China or England? In 1796 a country doctor scratched cowpox from a milkmaid's hand into an 8-year-old's arm, then exposed the boy to smallpox on purpose. Nothing happened, and the word he coined for it came from the Latin for cow.

intent: A medical historian telling it as a story: the village and the boy, the test that could have killed him, then the long line from one hand to a disease wiped off the planet.

v04.text: England. On 14 May 1796, Edward Jenner, a doctor in Berkeley, gave the very first.

v05.text: He scratched cowpox from a milkmaid's hand into the arm of 8-year-old James Phipps. Cow, in Latin, is vacca.

v06.text: Weeks later he exposed the boy to smallpox on purpose. Nothing happened. Smallpox killed 3 in 10 of its victims.

v07.text: In 1980, the WHO in Geneva declared smallpox eradicated, the only human disease ever wiped out.

research.topic: The first vaccine: Edward Jenner, Berkeley, Gloucestershire, England — on 14 May 1796 he inoculated 8-year-old James Phipps with cowpox matter from milkmaid Sarah Nelmes's hand, later challenged him with smallpox without effect, and coined 'vaccine' from vacca (Latin, cow). Smallpox killed about 30 % of those infected; the WHO declared it eradicated in 1980, the only human disease eradicated. Earlier variolation (China, Ottoman Empire) used smallpox itself and is not a vaccine.

myths.reality: Pasteur developed later vaccines (rabies, 1885) and named the technique in Jenner's honour; the first vaccine was Jenner's cowpox inoculation of 1796 in England.
China and the Ottoman world practised variolation — inoculation with smallpox itself, which was risky; Jenner's method used the harmless cowpox virus and is the first vaccine.

landscape.our_gap: Feed clips either praise Pasteur or show a needle over a stock photo; nobody puts Berkeley on the map, draws the line to Geneva and ties the Latin word to the result on screen.
